 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.488 Of 2010
Judgment:

This Criminal Revision Case is filed by the petitioner aggrieved by the judgment dated 03.03.2010 in Crl.A.No.7 of 2009, on the file of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, at Hyderabad, confirming the judgment dated 17.12.2008 in C.C.No.3251 of 2006, on the file of I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad.

entities.text: I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent- State.
Perused the record.
3. The revision petitioner was convicted for the offence under Section 420 of IPC and sentenced to suffer one year imprisonment.
4. Briefly, the case against the revision petitioner is that he was working as an Attender in Kakatiya Medical College.
He had taken an amount of Rs.20,000/- from P.W.2 on the ground that he would provide a job.
Having taken the said amount of Rs.20,000/-, he gave a letter Ex.P.2 addressed to P.W.1.
P.W.1 was working as Deputy Secretary to Government (L & O), General Administration Department, A.P.Secretariat.
P.W.2 carried the said letter -Ex.P.2 to P.W.1 on 20.05.2002 and handed over the same to P.W.1 stating that an amount of Rs.20,000/- was given to the accused for the purpose of providing a job.

P.W.1 then filed a complaint with the Police stating that this accused namely Sammaiah had earlier also sent letters to him through different persons having taken the amount from them with a promise that he would provide jobs to them.
P.W.3 is another witness who had given Rs.10,000/- to accused when the accused promised him that he would provide a job.

5. On the basis of the complaint, Ex.P.1 that was filed by P.W.1, the case was investigated and it was found in the course of investigation that the accused had taken money from different persons on the promise of providing them jobs and accordingly, he addressed letters to P.W.1.
6.
The Court below examined P.Ws.1 to 4 and marked Exs.P.1 to P.6 of which Ex.P.2 is the letter written by accused to P.W.1.

The trial Court found that the accused had induced P.Ws.3 and 4 with a promise to provide a job and had taken an amount of Rs.20,000/- from P.W.2 and an amount of Rs.10,000/- from P.W.3 and accordingly, accused was convicted.
The said conviction was questioned in the appeal before the Sessions Court.
The learned Sessions Judge found favour with the findings of the trial Court and confirmed the conviction.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that admittedly, Ex.P.2 letter was written by the daughter of the accused and she was not examined.

Further, according to the evidence of P.W.1, when P.W.1 questioned P.W.2 regarding the person sending the letter, P.W.2 took P.W.1 to the Office of Commissioner Panchayatraj, Tilak Road, Abids and had shown the accused.
The accused in fact was working in Kakatiya Medical College and the question of accused being present in the Office of Commissioner Panchayatraj at Abids does not arise.
For the said reasons, the conviction has to be set aside.

8. Having gone through the evidence of witnesses and documents, P.Ws.2 and 3 have specifically stated that the accused had taken amounts stating that he had talked to P.W.1 who was Deputy Secretary to Government (L & O), General Administration Department, A.P.Secretariat and he would give a job and accordingly, collected an amount of 20,000/- from P.W.2 and Rs.10,000/-
from P.W.3.
The said act of making a false promise of providing job and taking amount having knowledge that he cannot provide any job thereby, the said representation was with a intent to defraud P.Ws.1 and 2.
As such, ingredients of Section 420 of IPC are made out.
There are no grounds to interfere with the findings of the Courts below.

9. However, keeping in view that the incident is of the year, 2002 and nearly 22 years have passed by, this Court is inclined to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner.
10.
Accordingly, the Revision is partly allowed reducing the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
